Synopsis:
    Escalating Middle East conflict (US-Israel-Iran) is driving Brent crude toward US$110/bbl, pushing Australian fuel prices up 20-30c/litre. Rising oil prices are reinforcing inflation expectations, lifting US bond yields toward 5% and Australian 10-year yields to 15-year highs. The RBA is widely expected to hike rates again in September. Key concern beyond crude is refined product supply (especially diesel), with Strait of Hormuz disruption risk flagged as having no easy workaround. Brent is expected to trade in a US$70-100/bbl range until supply disruption dynamics stabilise.
